reader.requirement: For indexed files the SAME [RECORD] AREA clause obeys the Sequential I-O SAME clause (§1985:VII.2.13): operands are files of this program's FILE-CONTROL (SR1), not EXTERNAL (SR2), a file in at most one SAME AREA and one SAME RECORD AREA clause with SR3c's subset rule (SR3), organizations may be mixed (SR4); SAME RECORD AREA files share the current logical record as an implicit leftmost-aligned redefinition, all may be open together (GR2); SAME AREA files may not be open together (GR1, a constraint on the program).

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Edition.Year < 2002 changes only the REPORT-file row (§1985:XIII.2.4.3 SR2); an indexed file takes the SameFileKind.Other row, the same words and limits at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep of VersionConformancePass.cs for sameClause/SameClause found nothing; FileControlBinder.IoControl.cs read in full: the only edition test on the SAME path is SameOccurrenceRule's report-file row; the grammar rule sameClause is ungated
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for indexed files: 1985's SR1-SR4 and GR1-GR2 correspond to §2023:12.4.6.4 SR2, SR3, SR7, SR9 and GR1-GR2 for a non-report, non-sort file; only the report-file row differs and that is gated
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover mixed-organization legality, SAME RECORD AREA after CLOSE and legal clause combinations; the per-rule refusals (SR1, SR2, SR3a/b/c, single-operand clause) and a record-area round trip through two indexed files of unequal record length are not exercised at 85 for indexed files

reader.notes: Indexed files go through the one SAME binder with every other organization; the record area is linked as a synthesized REDEFINES of the first member's record. GR1's 'not valid to have more than one open' is a constraint on the program with no defined outcome, so no runtime check is required. Every refusal at --std 85 cites the §2023:12.4.6.4 rule rather than §1985:VII.2.13.3 (the words agree); this is cosmetic, not a conformance failure.
